name: Ibiden Co., Ltd.
blurb: Ibiden is a Japanese manufacturer headquartered in Gifu, Japan, that produces advanced IC substrates — the multilayered organic circuit boards connecting processor chips to their packages. It commands approximately 22% of the global ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film) substrate market and an estimated 70–80% of the highest-complexity segment used in leading AI GPUs and accelerators. Ibiden also manufactures silicon-carbide automotive components, but electronics — particularly AI substrates — now dominate its margin profile.
recent: Ibiden announced a ¥500 billion (approximately $3.3 billion) capital expenditure plan in February 2026 for AI substrate capacity expansion at its Gifu facilities, co-funded approximately 50% by advance payments from customers including Nvidia. Electronics-segment operating margins expanded to roughly 19% in fiscal 2025. The company faces a material constraint: ABF film, the proprietary substrate material, is sourced almost entirely from Ajinomoto Fine-Techno, which plans only a ~50% output increase by 2030.
